## How Do You Actually Compute a Proof That Your Controller Works?

You have designed a controller and tested it on a simulator. It looks good. But what about real hardware, sensor noise, model mismatch? The answer is not "try it and see"—that's expensive. Instead, you formulate *finding* the metric itself as an optimization: choose a metric and feedback gains simultaneously such that the closed-loop system is *provably* contracting. If the optimization succeeds, you have a certificate. If it fails, you know to design differently.

## Introduction and Qualitative Purpose

This chapter presents optimization-based workflows for obtaining metrics and gains with explicit contraction margins.

## In Laymans Terms

Do not trust performance alone; compute a stability certificate too.

## Geometric Intuition

Optimization chooses a local ruler and feedback direction fields so perturbations contract while task cost stays low.

## Representative Program

$$
(A-BK)^\top M + M(A-BK) \preceq -2\lambda M,\quad M\succ0.
$$

With variable substitutions, this admits LMI-based synthesis in important cases [@boyd1994].
